name: Ophthalmologist

pf.license.need: each ophthalmologist holds their own medical license from the state's medical board; an ophthalmic technician holds one only where the state licenses technicians
pf.license.who: each person; the practice too where the state's form registers eye practices or their owners
pf.license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply, or the owner sends it; the practice's registration and any mobile permit number come from the owner. The owner may leave a number out
pf.license.check: Rosie does not look up, check or verify a license number. The owner gives it, and it is shown where the state asks
pf.license.blocks: no booking is held or refused because of a license: the owner states it, and that is the record
pf.license.away: eye visits at a care home, a school or a home only where the state's rules allow mobile or portable eye care; a mobile or portable permit where the state's form asks for one (a switch)
pf.license.sedation: no sedation or general anesthesia is booked by Rosie. The practice plans any sedation itself, with the patient, by phone; Rosie never prices, confirms or moves it
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking; every company in Rosie's chain signs one with Rosie
pf.license.renewals: if the owner records an expiry date, Rosie reminds the owner 30 days before it; Rosie does not check the license
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it; the owner states it, and Rosie does not check it

pf.services.shape: visit types in an exam room, each with a set length; a first visit has a technician's tests, then the ophthalmologist's exam; a procedure is planned after the tests and booked as its own visit; every visit needs a free exam room
pf.services.examples: the example practices' own prices (Lee Eye Clinic and Lee Home Eye Care), not a standard; a plan pays its own share for eye care, up to its yearly limit, and the patient's share is an estimate

list.name: New patient eye consult (pressure and retina checks, then the ophthalmologist's exam)
list.kind: one price; the plan's estimate is shown when a plan pays
list.length: 60 min: 30 with the technician (tests and photos), then 30 with the ophthalmologist
list.after: the patient's share at the front desk
list.note: new-patient times are kept apart (Sam's booking rules)

list.name: Laser treatment (one eye, planned after the tests)
list.length: 45 min, with drops and a check after
list.after: the $100 rest at the chair, after the treatment
list.note: no sedation here: sedation is planned by phone and is never booked by Rosie

list.name: Eye injection visit (the medicine is ordered by the ophthalmologist)
list.note: no plan pays the injection visit in full; the plan's share is shown first

list.name: Eye imaging, quoted from photos first (a scan of the retina or the optic nerve)
list.length: 2 visits: the photos, then the scan
list.before: a $20 deposit once the ophthalmologist's quote is OK'd
list.after: the rest ($70) at the front desk, at the scan
list.note: the ophthalmologist OKs the quote before any deposit

list.name: Eye problem visit (red, sore, itchy or watery eyes, or a new floater)
list.price: the $25 check is promised; any test or drops are priced at the chair (the example: $110 in all)
list.note: the owner OKs same-day times first

list.name: Lens check during an eye visit
list.note: a medical plan may not pay it, so the share is shown first

list.name: Eye pressure check, paid in full when booked
Eye check and follow-up at a care home
list.kind: one price; the plan's share when a plan pays
list.length: 45 min, with a portable exam kit
list.where: at the customer's place (a care home or a home)
list.before: nothing taken when a plan pays; private pay gets Rosfield's bill after the visit
list.after: the office bills the plan its own way; private pay: Rosie texts the bill

list.name: Eye problem at a care home
list.price: the $89 eye check is promised; any test or drops are priced at the visit (the example: $245 in all)

list.name: Low-vision aids (magnifiers and special glasses), quoted after a first exam
list.price: $640 (the example practice's price, quoted from the first exam's notes)
list.length: 2 visits: the exam and the fitting
list.before: a $160 deposit when the quote is OK'd (25%)
list.after: Rosie texts the bill for the $480 rest when the ophthalmologist texts DONE

list.name: School eye screening day
list.price: set with the school: free to families, or billed to each child's plan
list.length: a whole morning, one portable kit
list.after: the office bills plans its own way
list.note: each child needs a parent's or guardian's signed consent on the secure page

pf.services.capacity: one patient per exam room; the portable exam kit is booked like a person
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the patient is always there
pf.services.online: none: an eye exam, a test or a procedure needs the office's own equipment; a question by video is answered by the office, not booked as a visit

beforeTimes: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: the practice's own visit types only (a new patient consult, a laser treatment, an injection, an imaging scan, or an eye problem visit), never a symptom typed into the AI
a vision or medical plan (its name only) or paying yourself
afterTime: anything the practice should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a care home visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the ophthalmologist
securePage: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the plan card
health history: medicines, blood thinners, allergies, eye conditions, diabetes
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)
pf.questions.neverAsked: symptoms, reasons or results are never asked or typed in the AI chat

stop.words: sudden vision loss, sudden flashes of light, or a shadow or curtain across the vision
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911. Don't wait for an eye visit.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words are repeated if a same-day request is declined, and if it starts before a booked visit (the visit stays booked and the owner is told)

stop.words: a chemical splash in the eye, or something stuck in it
stop.say: Rinse a chemical splash with clean running water right away, and call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 or 911. Don't rub something stuck in the eye: go to the emergency room or call 911.
stop.booking: no booking; the words are fixed and the same for everyone

stop.words: an eye hit hard or cut, or sudden bad eye pain with a headache or throwing up
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911.

goOn.words: red, itchy, sore or dry eyes with nothing else
goOn.what: matched to the practice's own eye problem visit; Rosie never judges how urgent it is, and same-day times need the owner's OK

pf.safety.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.name: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before any test), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered, some services only, not covered, or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free)

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; sent within 1 business day (the example practice's rule), or sooner where the rules require it
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: A signed procedure consent
steps.when: on the secure page, before the laser or injection visit, with the price and the deposit shown first
steps.who: every procedure patient, and the parent or guardian for a child
steps.result: not signed by the procedure visit: the visit waits; Sam moves it or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The care home's OK
steps.who: the host place agrees to host the visits
steps.result: no OK: no times at that place

pf.first_steps.prep: bring your glasses, your medicine list and a photo ID; a dilated exam blurs the eyes for a few hours, so a ride home is needed; at a care home: the medicine list ready with the nurse

pf.visit.checkIn: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or school: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or staff member named on the booking
pf.visit.beforeWork: the technician does the pre-tests (vision, eye pressure, imaging) first; the ophthalmologist reads the health history and checks for changes before any procedure
pf.visit.dilation: only the ophthalmologist decides on dilating drops; they take about 20 minutes to work, and the eyes stay blurry and light-sensitive for a few hours, so a ride home is required
pf.visit.changes: an extra test or drops are priced and OK'd before they're done; a medical problem found at a routine exam may move the visit to the medical plan, with the share shown first; a laser or an injection is booked as its own visit only with the patient's yes
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the ophthalmologist's notes, scans and prescriptions stay in the practice's own records, never in Rosie or a text
pf.visit.away: a portable exam kit (a light, a chair and a camera); the care home's nurse is told when the visit is done

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking for a new patient consult or an eye problem visit (the practice bills vision and medical plans); a card saved only where the practice turns on its missed-visit fee; a laser treatment: a $40 deposit when booked, and the rest at the chair; an injection visit: paid in full when booked; imaging from photos: a $20 deposit once the quote is OK'd; at a care home: nothing taken when a plan pays, a $160 deposit for low-vision aids once the quote is OK'd, the rest on Rosfield's bill
pf.money.plans: the plans the practice takes (its own list); the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it: active or not, what it pays for eye care and up to what yearly limit; the patient's share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay patient is told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.fees: the missed-visit fee: $20 at the example practice, only when the owner turns it on; a card is saved for it, and the same fee applies to every patient who may be charged one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch: no fee ever for patients whose plan or the state's rules bar one (like Medicaid, where that applies), or whom the owner marks fee-free; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.after: claims sent by the practice; the patient pays their share at the front desk, its own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the practice, not by Rosie's text; at a care home, the practice bills its own way, and private pay gets the bill Rosie texts
pf.money.rosfield: the business pays Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking, as every business does (the $2 is counted when the visit's check-in code is entered; no visit, no $2); card payments also cost Stripe's own card fee
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form; fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules

pf.messages.never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, the results, the medicines or the ophthalmologist's name (when the ophthalmologist comes to a care home, school or home, the name stays, for the door check); scans and results never go through Rosie
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the patient's initials only (A.M., never Alex M.)
pf.messages.minors: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
pf.messages.decider: for an adult who can't consent, the texts go to the person who decides, and the code to whoever meets the ophthalmologist

pf.staff.licenses: each ophthalmologist's own medical license, per state; an ophthalmic technician's own license only where the state licenses technicians
pf.staff.skills: ophthalmologists: exams, laser treatments, injections, eye surgery referrals, low-vision aids and prescriptions; ophthalmic technicians: pre-tests, imaging, drop teaching and the work the state allows; only people cleared for mobile visits go to care homes and schools
pf.staff.supervision: a technician's pre-tests are read by the ophthalmologist; which tests a technician may run comes from the state form (a switch)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs same-day eye problem times, quotes over $500, and anything a technician flags
pf.staff.standIn: a technician out: the ophthalmologist runs the pre-tests, or new times; the ophthalmologist out: another ophthalmologist takes the visit, or new times with no fee
pf.staff.away: the team at a care home or school is the people cleared for mobile visits, with the portable exam kit; sedation is never given at a care home or a home

pf.rules.records: eye records are kept by the practice for as long as the state's rules require (a child's records may be kept longer); a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the practice's records
pf.rules.copies: a patient's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the practice, and on a visit away from it
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.host: a visit at a care home or school only under the host's written OK, and the host's sign-in rules; visit days at a host's place (S1-58) need the host's standing OK on file; the example's care home visits are booked one resident at a time under the care home's OK, so no visit days are set
pf.rules.ads: no free-exam or price claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form

pf.edges.lateArrival: more than 15 minutes late: still seen, but part of the visit may move to another day (the practice decides; Rosie never changes the booking itself)
pf.edges.standIn: an ophthalmologist or technician out: a stand-in who may do that part, or new times with no fee
pf.edges.forms: a form not done by its due date: one reminder, then Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page before any test), moves it, or cancels with no fee (A7-74, B7-61)
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.noRide: a patient with no ride home after dilating drops: the ophthalmologist may use a retina photo instead, or the patient waits until the drops wear off; Rosie only puts the ride note in the reminder
pf.edges.twoBookings: a patient with a procedure and a check both open: Rosie asks which one before any change
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about medicine or eye drops before the visit goes to the ophthalmologist; Rosie gives no advice
pf.edges.careHome: the resident is out (at the hospital, or asleep): the nurse says so, and the visit moves with no fee
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way
pf.edges.urgent: no service is sent now and nobody is on call (S2-30, S2-31): an eye problem gets the soonest same-day time, with the owner's OK; vision loss, flashes or a curtain over the vision get the 911 words

B.other: Others (the care home's nurse, a school nurse, a parent or guardian, a family member who pays, a plan)

story.A: Sam Lee, an ophthalmologist, signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books a new patient eye consult with Hana at Lee Eye Clinic for Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am. Names: Sam Lee, an ophthalmologist, owns Lee Home Eye Care LLC (the master's main company: mobile eye care at care homes and schools, 75 Mill Rd) and Lee Eye Clinic LLC (the second company: the office, 520 Harbor Ave). Flow A is at the office; flow B at Riverside care home, 64 Linden Rd, where Alex lives. Staff: Hana (ophthalmologist) and Ivan (technician) at the office; Tomas (ophthalmologist) and Gia (technician) on the mobile team.
